shapes.description: Turns Windows Firewall on or off for the {profile} network profile. Windows picks the profile from the network the computer is connected to. Leave it unset to keep the firewall on, which is the default.

valueHelp.true: Windows Firewall is on for the {profile} profile.
valueHelp.false: Windows Firewall is off for the {profile} profile, so every port is open.

valueHelp.false: Windows asks the user when the firewall blocks a new app.

shapes.description: Whether the firewall writes dropped packets to its log for the {profile} profile. Turn it on while you troubleshoot a blocked connection. Leave it unset to keep logging off.

valueHelp.true: Dropped packets are written to the firewall log.
valueHelp.false: Dropped packets are not logged.

shapes.description: Whether the firewall writes allowed connections to its log for the {profile} profile. The log grows quickly, so use it only while troubleshooting. Leave it unset to keep logging off.

valueHelp.true: Allowed connections are written to the firewall log.
valueHelp.false: Allowed connections are not logged.

shapes.description: Where the firewall log for the {profile} profile is written. The folder must exist and be writable by the firewall service. Leave it empty for %SystemRoot%\System32\LogFiles\Firewall\pfirewall.log.
Maximum size of the firewall log for the {profile} profile, in kilobytes. When it is full, older entries are overwritten. Leave it unset for 4,096 KB (4 MB).
What Microsoft Defender does by default with threats of this severity. Choose Quarantine or Remove for a hands-off device. Leave it unset (NULL) to use the action Defender recommends.

valueHelp.1: Clean: Defender tries to repair the infected file.
valueHelp.2: Quarantine: the file is moved to a safe store where it cannot run.
valueHelp.6: Allow: the threat is ignored and allowed to run.
valueHelp.8: User defined: the user picks the action each time.
valueHelp.9: No action: Defender only reports the threat.
valueHelp.10: Block: the threat is stopped from running.
valueHelp.NULL: Use the default action Defender recommends for this threat.

ComputerName.description: The network name of the computer, up to 15 letters, digits and hyphens, not only digits. Use * to let Windows make a random name. Leave it unset and Windows also makes a random name.

TimeZone.description: The Windows time zone id, which sets the clock offset and the daylight saving rules. Pick the zone where the computer is used. Leave it unset and Windows uses the zone that matches the install language or asks during the out-of-box experience.

DisableAutoDaylightTimeSet.description: Whether Windows moves the clock automatically for daylight saving time. Turn it on only when another system sets the clock, for example a lab that must stay on standard time. Leave it unset to follow daylight saving time.

valueHelp.true: The clock does not change for daylight saving time.
valueHelp.false: The clock moves automatically for daylight saving time.

RegisteredOrganization.description: The organization name shown in About and in winver. It is only informational. Leave it empty to show nothing.

RegisteredOwner.description: The owner name shown in About and in winver. It is only informational. Leave it empty to show nothing.

ProductKey.description: The product key applied in the specialize pass, which can differ from the key used to install. Use a volume (MAK) or retail key to activate, or a generic key to only pick the edition. Generic keys only select an edition during Setup; they never activate Windows.

CopyProfile.description: Copies the customized built-in Administrator profile to the default user profile during sysprep. Use it after customizing the desktop in audit mode so every new user gets those settings. Leave it unset to keep the stock default profile.

valueHelp.true: The Administrator profile becomes the default profile for new users.
valueHelp.false: New users get the stock default profile.

risk.reason: Anything in the Administrator profile, including cached data, is copied to every new user.

AutoLogon/Enabled.description: Signs in automatically with the account below after Setup, for the number of times in LogonCount. Use it to run first sign-in scripts without someone typing a password. Leave it unset so Windows shows the sign-in screen.

valueHelp.true: Windows signs in automatically with the account below.
valueHelp.false: Windows shows the sign-in screen as normal.

risk.reason: The automatic sign-in password is kept in the registry until the count runs out.

AutoLogon/LogonCount.description: How many times Windows signs in automatically before it stops. Each restart uses one. Leave it unset for a single automatic sign-in.

AutoLogon/Username.description: The account that signs in automatically, usually Administrator or an account created in LocalAccounts. It must exist when the sign-in happens. Leave it empty to turn automatic sign-in off.

AutoLogon/Domain.description: The domain of the automatic sign-in account, or the computer name for a local account. Leave it empty for a local account. Domain accounts work only after the computer has joined the domain.

AutoLogon/Password/Value.description: The password of the automatic sign-in account. Windows stores it in the registry until the sign-in count runs out. Leave it empty for an account without a password.

UserAccounts/AdministratorPassword/Value.description: The password of the built-in Administrator account. Setting it skips the password prompt and lets you sign in as Administrator. Leave it empty and the Administrator account stays disabled on client editions.

UserAccounts/LocalAccounts/LocalAccount/.description: The user name of a local account created during Setup, up to 20 characters. It cannot contain characters such as \ / [ ] : ; | = , + * ? < > ". Each account in the list needs a unique name.
The full name shown on the sign-in screen and in Settings. It can contain spaces. Leave it empty to show the user name.
A note stored with the account and shown in Computer Management. It is only informational. Leave it empty for no note.
The local group the account joins, usually Administrators or Users. Separate several groups with semicolons. Leave it empty and the account joins Users.
The password of this local account. Use a strong password, or a temporary one the user changes later. Leave it empty for an account without a password, which Windows only allows for local sign-in.

UserAccounts/DomainAccounts/DomainAccoun.description: The domain whose accounts or groups are added to local groups. The computer must already be joined to it. Use the NetBIOS or DNS domain name.
A domain user or group to add to the local group below. It must exist in the domain above. A group such as Domain Admins is a common choice.
The local group that the domain account joins, such as Administrators or Remote Desktop Users. It must be an existing local group. Leave it empty and Windows uses Users.

OOBE/HideEULAPage.description: Hides the Windows license page during the out-of-box experience. You accept the license on behalf of the user when you turn it on. Leave it unset and the user must accept the license.

valueHelp.true: The license page is skipped; the license counts as accepted.
valueHelp.false: The user sees the license page and must accept it.

OOBE/HideLocalAccountScreen.description: Hides the page that creates a local account during the out-of-box experience. Use it when the answer file already creates accounts or sets the Administrator password. Leave it unset to show the page.

valueHelp.true: The create account page is skipped.
valueHelp.false: The user is asked to create an account.

OOBE/HideOEMRegistrationScreen.description: Hides the device maker registration page during the out-of-box experience. Most organizations turn it on. Leave it unset to show the page when the image has one.

valueHelp.true: The OEM registration page is skipped.
valueHelp.false: The OEM registration page is shown when the image has one.

OOBE/HideOnlineAccountScreens.description: Hides the Microsoft account and work account sign-in pages during the out-of-box experience. Use it for local or domain accounts. Leave it unset to offer online accounts.

valueHelp.true: The online account pages are skipped.
valueHelp.false: The user is offered a Microsoft or work account sign-in.

OOBE/HideWirelessSetupInOOBE.description: Hides the Wi-Fi network page during the out-of-box experience. Use it on wired or offline builds. Leave it unset to let the user pick a network.

valueHelp.true: The Wi-Fi page is skipped.
valueHelp.false: The user can pick a Wi-Fi network.

OOBE/ProtectYourPC.description: Answers the privacy and update settings page of the out-of-box experience. Use 3 for kiosks and labs that must not send data, or 1 to accept the recommended settings. Leave it unset and the user is asked.

valueHelp.1: Use the recommended settings, including automatic updates and diagnostics.
valueHelp.3: Turn off the optional settings; the user can change them later.

OOBE/NetworkLocation.description: The network location chosen for the first network on older Windows releases. Work and Home allow discovery; Other is the public profile. Leave it unset and Windows asks or uses the public profile.

valueHelp.Home: Private network: the computer can be discovered and share files.
valueHelp.Work: Work network: like Home, for an office.
valueHelp.Other: Public network: discovery and sharing are off.

OOBE/SkipMachineOOBE.description: An old switch that skipped the whole machine part of the out-of-box experience. Windows no longer supports it and may leave the computer unconfigured. Use the Hide settings instead.

valueHelp.true: Skips the machine out-of-box experience (unsupported on current Windows).
valueHelp.false: The machine out-of-box experience runs as normal.

risk.reason: Deprecated; current Windows may skip required steps.

OOBE/SkipUserOOBE.description: An old switch that skipped the user part of the out-of-box experience. Windows no longer supports it. Use the Hide settings instead.

valueHelp.true: Skips the user out-of-box experience (unsupported on current Windows).
valueHelp.false: The user out-of-box experience runs as normal.

risk.reason: Deprecated; current Windows may skip required steps.

OOBE/UnattendEnableRetailDemo.description: Puts the device in retail demo mode for store displays. Never use it on a computer people will work on, because demo mode resets the device. Leave it unset for a normal install.

valueHelp.true: The device starts in retail demo mode.
valueHelp.false: The device installs normally.

risk.reason: Retail demo mode wipes user content and is meant for store displays only.

OEMInformation/Manufacturer.description: The manufacturer name shown in Settings, System, About. It helps users know who supports the computer. Leave it empty to show the hardware maker reported by the firmware.

OEMInformation/Model.description: The model name shown in Settings, System, About. Recent Windows versions read the model from the firmware instead. Leave it empty to show the firmware model.

OEMInformation/SupportHours.description: The hours when support is available, shown in Settings, System, About. Write it the way users read it. Leave it empty to hide the line.

OEMInformation/SupportPhone.description: The support phone number shown in Settings, System, About. Include the country code for devices that travel. Leave it empty to hide the line.

OEMInformation/SupportURL.description: The support web page shown in Settings, System, About and in the Get Help app. Use an https address. Leave it empty to hide the link.

OEMInformation/Logo.description: Path on the installed computer to a 120 by 120 pixel BMP logo shown in Settings, System, About. Copy the file with $OEM$ folders or a command first. Leave it empty for no logo.

Themes/WindowColor.description: The accent color for title bars, Start and other surfaces, written as 0xAARRGGBB or Automatic. Windows adjusts very dark or very light colors so text stays readable. Leave it unset for the default blue.

Themes/DesktopBackground.description: Path on the installed computer to the default wallpaper image. The file must already exist when the user signs in. Leave it empty for the Windows wallpaper.

Themes/ThemeName.description: The name of your custom theme as it appears in Personalization. It labels the theme built from these settings. Leave it empty when you do not ship a theme.

FirstLogonCommands/SynchronousCommand/Co.description: The command line that runs when a user signs in for the first time, one command after another. It runs as that user, so it cannot install machine-wide software without rights. Quote paths that contain spaces.

FirstLogonCommands/SynchronousCommand/Or.description: Position of this command in the first sign-in list, from 1 to 500. Commands run in ascending order and each number must be unique. The studio renumbers commands when you reorder them.

FirstLogonCommands/SynchronousCommand/De.description: A short label for the command. It is only informational. Leave it empty if the command line explains itself.

FirstLogonCommands/SynchronousCommand/Re.description: Tells Windows that the command opens a window the user must answer. Windows then waits for the user instead of continuing. Leave it unset for commands that run on their own.

valueHelp.true: Windows waits for the user to answer the command.
valueHelp.false: The command runs without user interaction.

LogonCommands/AsynchronousCommand/Comman.description: The command line that starts at each of the first sign-ins, without waiting for it. Use it for long-running tools. Quote paths that contain spaces.

LogonCommands/AsynchronousCommand/Order.description: Position of this command in the list, from 1 to 500. Commands start in ascending order without waiting for each other. Each number must be unique.

LogonCommands/AsynchronousCommand/Descri.description: A short label for the command. It is only informational. Leave it empty if the command line explains itself.

LogonCommands/AsynchronousCommand/Requir.description: Tells Windows that the command opens a window the user must answer. Windows then waits for the user instead of continuing. Leave it unset for commands that run on their own.

valueHelp.true: Windows waits for the user to answer the command.
valueHelp.false: The command runs without user interaction.

OEMInformation/HelpCustomized.description: An old switch that said the device maker customized Windows Help. Current Windows ignores it; set SupportURL or SupportAppURL instead. Leave it unset.

valueHelp.true: Marks Help as customized (ignored on current Windows).
valueHelp.false: Help is not customized.

OEMInformation/TradeinURL.description: A web page about trading in the device, shown in the Get Help app. Use an https address. Leave it empty to hide the link.

OEMInformation/RecycleURL.description: A web page about recycling the device, shown in the Get Help app. Use an https address. Leave it empty to hide the link.

OEMInformation/SupportAppURL.description: A link that opens the device maker support app from the Get Help app. Use the protocol link the app registers. Leave it empty to hide the link.

OEMInformation/SupportProvider.description: The name of your support app or website, shown next to the support link in Get Help. Use a short name people recognise. Leave it empty to show the manufacturer name.

OOBE/OEMAppId.description: The app user model ID of a device maker app the out-of-box experience can hand off to. Only device makers set it. Leave it empty for none.

OOBE/VMModeOptimizations/SkipWinREInitia.description: Skips preparing the recovery environment when Windows runs as a virtual machine. It saves time on disposable VMs that never need recovery. Leave it unset to prepare it as normal.

valueHelp.true: The recovery environment is not prepared in VM mode.
valueHelp.false: The recovery environment is prepared as normal.

OOBE/VMModeOptimizations/SkipAdministrat.description: Keeps the built-in Administrator profile when Windows runs as a virtual machine. It saves time on VMs that reuse that profile. Leave it unset to remove it as normal.

OOBE/VMModeOptimizations/SkipNotifyUILan.description: Skips telling apps about a display language change when Windows runs as a virtual machine. It saves time on VMs. Leave it unset for the normal notification.

Themes/CustomDefaultThemeFile.description: Path to a .theme file once used as the default theme. Current Windows no longer accepts a theme file here. Leave it empty.

Themes/ScreenSaver.description: The screen saver of the default theme on older Windows releases. Current Windows ignores it. Leave it empty.

Themes/BrandIcon.description: Path to an image shown in Personalization next to the custom theme name. The file must exist on the installed computer. Leave it empty for no icon.

Themes/UWPAppsUseLightTheme.description: Chooses light or dark mode for apps by default. Users can still change it in Settings. Leave it unset for light mode.

valueHelp.true: Apps use the light theme.
valueHelp.false: Apps use the dark theme.

Themes/DefaultThemesOff.description: Hides the themes that ship with Windows so users only see your custom theme. Use it with ThemeName. Leave it unset to show every theme.

valueHelp.true: Built-in themes are hidden.
valueHelp.false: Built-in themes are shown.

VisualEffects/FontSmoothing.description: How the screen smooths font edges on older Windows releases. Current Windows always uses ClearType. Leave it unset.

valueHelp.Standard: Windows picks after a performance test.

VisualEffects/SystemDefaultBackgroundCol.description: A background color number for the old Start screen. Current Windows ignores it. Leave it empty.

ShowWindowsLive.description: Shows or hides Windows Live links on the old Start menu. This applies to Windows 7 era images only. Leave it unset.

valueHelp.true: Windows Live links are shown.
valueHelp.false: Windows Live links are hidden.

ConvertibleSlateModePromptPreference.description: Whether a convertible device asks before switching to tablet mode when the keyboard is removed. Only 2 in 1 devices use it. Leave it unset for the Windows default.

valueHelp.0: Windows does not ask before switching.
valueHelp.1: Windows asks before switching to tablet mode.

SignInMode.description: Which mode a tablet capable device starts in after sign-in. Use Desktop for laptops used like PCs. Leave it unset for the Windows default.

valueHelp.0: Start in tablet mode.
valueHelp.2: Start in the mode last used.

OEMName.description: The device maker name shown on the group of pinned Start tiles. Only applies to older Start layouts. Leave it empty for no group name.

UserData/AcceptEula.description: Accepts the Windows license terms during Setup so the license page does not appear. You accept the terms on behalf of the organization. Leave it unset and Setup stops at the license page.

valueHelp.true: The license terms are accepted; Setup does not stop.
valueHelp.false: Setup shows the license page and waits.

UserData/ProductKey/Key.description: The product key used to install, which also picks the edition from the media. A generic key installs an edition without activating it. Generic keys only select an edition during Setup; they never activate Windows.

UserData/ProductKey/WillShowUI.description: When Setup shows the product key page. OnError shows it only if the key is missing or wrong. Leave it unset for OnError.

valueHelp.Always: Setup always shows the product key page.
valueHelp.OnError: Setup shows the page only when the key is missing or invalid.
valueHelp.Never: Setup never shows the page; a bad key stops Setup.

UserData/FullName.description: The name of the person or team the copy of Windows is licensed to. It is only informational. Leave it empty to skip.

UserData/Organization.description: The organization the copy of Windows is licensed to. It is only informational. Leave it empty to skip.

DiskConfiguration/Disk/WillWipeDisk.description: Erases every partition on this disk before creating the new ones. Use it for clean installs on new or repurposed disks. Leave it unset to keep existing partitions.

valueHelp.true: Every partition and all data on this disk are erased.
valueHelp.false: Existing partitions are kept; only the listed changes are made.

risk.reason: All data on the disk is destroyed.

DiskConfiguration/Disk/DiskID.description: The number of the disk to configure; 0 is the first disk Windows PE finds. Disk numbers can change when you add USB drives, so unplug extras. The studio disk canvas edits this for you.

DiskConfiguration/Disk/CreatePartitions/.description: Size of the new partition in megabytes. Leave Extend on for the last partition instead of a size. The percentage is shown against the disk size you enter in the widget.
Makes this partition fill the rest of the disk. Use it on the last partition only, and do not also set Size. Leave it unset to use the Size value.

valueHelp.true: The partition grows to fill the rest of the disk.
valueHelp.false: The partition uses the Size value.

DiskConfiguration/Disk/CreatePartitions/.description: The partition type. A UEFI disk needs an EFI partition, an MSR partition and a Primary partition for Windows. Leave it unset for Primary.

valueHelp.Primary: A normal data partition, used for Windows itself.
valueHelp.EFI: The EFI system partition that holds the UEFI boot files (FAT32, about 100 to 300 MB).
valueHelp.Extended: A container for logical partitions on MBR disks only.
valueHelp.Logical: A partition inside an extended partition, MBR disks only.
valueHelp.MSR: The Microsoft reserved partition required on GPT disks (16 MB, never formatted).

DiskConfiguration/Disk/CreatePartitions/.description: The order in which this partition is created, starting at 1. Partitions are created in this order from the start of the disk. Each number must be unique on the disk.

DiskConfiguration/Disk/ModifyPartitions/.description: The file system to format the partition with. EFI partitions use FAT32; Windows partitions use NTFS. Leave it unset to keep the partition unformatted.

valueHelp.NTFS: Format with NTFS, used for Windows and data partitions.
valueHelp.FAT32: Format with FAT32, used for the EFI system partition.

DiskConfiguration/Disk/ModifyPartitions/.description: The drive letter given to the partition in Windows PE and in the installed system. The Windows partition is usually C. Leave it unset for no letter.
The volume label shown in File Explorer, up to 32 characters for NTFS and 11 for FAT32. It is only informational. Leave it empty for no label.
Marks the partition as the active boot partition on BIOS (MBR) computers. UEFI computers ignore it. Leave it unset unless you install on a BIOS computer.

valueHelp.true: The partition is marked active so BIOS firmware boots from it.
valueHelp.false: The partition is not marked active.

DiskConfiguration/Disk/ModifyPartitions/.description: A partition type GUID (GPT) or type number (MBR) to set, for example the recovery partition type. Setup uses it to hide utility partitions. Leave it empty for a normal partition.

DiskConfiguration/WillShowUI.description: When Setup shows the disk page. OnError shows it only if the disk settings fail. Leave it unset for OnError.

valueHelp.Always: Setup always shows the disk page.
valueHelp.OnError: Setup shows the disk page only when the settings fail.
valueHelp.Never: Setup never shows the page; a failure stops Setup.

ImageInstall/OSImage/InstallTo/DiskID.description: The disk to install Windows on; 0 is the first disk. It must match a disk in DiskConfiguration or an existing disk. The disk canvas sets it when you mark the target.

ImageInstall/OSImage/InstallTo/Partition.description: The partition to install Windows on, counting from 1 on that disk. On the usual UEFI layout it is 3 (after EFI and MSR). The disk canvas sets it when you mark the target.

ImageInstall/OSImage/InstallFrom/MetaDat.description: How the image in install.wim is picked: by index number, by name or by description. Index is the most reliable. The value below must match the key you choose.

valueHelp./IMAGE/INDEX: Pick the image by its index number, for example 1.
valueHelp./IMAGE/NAME: Pick the image by its name, for example Windows 11 Pro.
valueHelp./IMAGE/DESCRIPTION: Pick the image by its description text.

ImageInstall/OSImage/InstallFrom/MetaDat.description: The value that selects the image in install.wim: an index number, an image name or a description, depending on the key. Run dism /Get-ImageInfo on the media to list them. A wrong value stops Setup.

ImageInstall/OSImage/InstallFrom/Path.description: The path of the install.wim or install.esd file, local or on a network share. Leave it empty to use the image on the install media. Network paths need credentials.

ImageInstall/OSImage/WillShowUI.description: When Setup shows the page that picks an image and partition. OnError shows it only when the settings fail. Leave it unset for OnError.

valueHelp.Always: Setup always shows the image page.
valueHelp.OnError: Setup shows the page only when the settings fail.
valueHelp.Never: Setup never shows the page; a failure stops Setup.

EnableFirewall.description: Turns Windows Firewall on in Windows PE during Setup. Keep it on unless a deployment tool must connect in to Windows PE. Leave it unset to keep the firewall on.

valueHelp.true: The firewall is on in Windows PE.
valueHelp.false: The firewall is off in Windows PE.

risk.reason: Windows PE runs with an open firewall during Setup.

EnableNetwork.description: Starts networking in Windows PE so Setup can reach shares and updates. Turn it on when the image or drivers come from the network. Leave it unset to keep networking off during the Windows PE stage.

valueHelp.true: Networking starts in Windows PE.
valueHelp.false: Windows PE runs without networking.

Restart.description: What Windows PE does after the windowsPE pass finishes. Shutdown is useful when you capture or move the disk before first boot. Leave it unset to restart.

valueHelp.Restart: The computer restarts and continues Setup.
valueHelp.Shutdown: The computer shuts down after Windows PE.

LogPath.description: A folder where Setup writes its logs during Windows PE. It must be writable, for example a RAM drive or a share. Leave it empty for the default Panther folder.

DynamicUpdate/Enable.description: Lets Setup download the latest Setup and compatibility updates before installing. Turn it off for offline or repeatable builds. Leave it unset to keep Dynamic Update off.

valueHelp.true: Setup downloads updates before it installs.
valueHelp.false: Setup uses only what is on the media.

ComplianceCheck/DisplayReport.description: When Setup shows the compatibility report during an upgrade. Leave it unset for OnError.

valueHelp.OnError: The report appears only when a problem blocks the upgrade.
valueHelp.Never: The report never appears; a blocking problem stops Setup.

UseConfigurationSet.description: Tells Setup to use the files of a configuration set next to the answer file, such as $OEM$ folders. Turn it on when you built a configuration set with Windows SIM. Leave it unset otherwise.

valueHelp.true: Setup copies the configuration set files.
valueHelp.false: Setup ignores configuration set folders.

PageFile/Path.description: Path of the page file Windows PE uses during Setup. Only computers with very little memory need it. Leave it empty for the default.

valueHelp.true: Windows goes to the first partition with enough space.
valueHelp.false: Windows goes to the partition set in InstallTo.

WindowsDeploymentServices/ImageSelection.description: The file name of the image to install from the Windows Deployment Services server, such as install.wim. It applies only when Setup installs from a Windows Deployment Services server. Leave it empty and the user picks an image.

The image group on the Windows Deployment Services server that holds the image. It applies only when Setup installs from a Windows Deployment Services server. Leave it empty and the user picks an image.

The name of the image to install from the Windows Deployment Services server. It applies only when Setup installs from a Windows Deployment Services server. Leave it empty and the user picks an image.
The disk to install the server image on; 0 is the first disk. It applies only when Setup installs from a Windows Deployment Services server. Leave it unset and the user picks the disk.
The partition to install the server image on, counting from 1. It applies only when Setup installs from a Windows Deployment Services server. Leave it empty and the user picks the partition.
When Setup shows the Windows Deployment Services image page. It applies only when Setup installs from a Windows Deployment Services server. Leave it unset for OnError.

valueHelp.Always: The image page is always shown.
valueHelp.OnError: The image page is shown only when the settings fail.
valueHelp.Never: The image page is never shown.

WindowsDeploymentServices/Login/WillShow.description: When Setup shows the Windows Deployment Services sign-in page. It applies only when Setup installs from a Windows Deployment Services server. Leave it unset for OnError.

valueHelp.Always: The sign-in page is always shown.
valueHelp.OnError: The sign-in page is shown only when the credentials fail.
valueHelp.Never: The sign-in page is never shown.

InputLocale.description: The keyboard layouts and input methods, as a language tag such as en-US or a pair such as 0409:00000409. Separate several with semicolons; the first is the default. Leave it unset to use the layout that matches the display language.

SystemLocale.description: The language used by programs that are not Unicode, and the default code page. Change it only when such programs show garbled text. Leave it unset to match the display language.

UILanguage.description: The display language of menus, dialogs and messages. The language pack must be on the image. Leave it unset to keep the language of the image.

UILanguageFallback.description: The language used for text that is not translated in a partly localized display language. Usually en-US. Leave it unset to use the image default.

UserLocale.description: The formats for dates, times, numbers and currency. It can differ from the display language, for example English text with Hong Kong formats. Leave it unset to match the display language.

InputLocale.description: The keyboard layouts and input methods, as a language tag such as en-US or a pair such as 0409:00000409. Separate several with semicolons; the first is the default. Leave it unset to use the layout that matches the Setup language.

SystemLocale.description: The language used by programs that are not Unicode, and the default code page. Change it only when such programs show garbled text. Leave it unset to match the display language.

UILanguage.description: The display language of the installed system when no other setting overrides it. The language pack must be on the image. Leave it unset to keep the language of the image.

UILanguageFallback.description: The language used for text that is not translated in a partly localized display language. Usually en-US. Leave it unset to use the image default.

UserLocale.description: The formats for dates, times, numbers and currency. It can differ from the display language, for example English text with Hong Kong formats. Leave it unset to match the display language.

SetupUILanguage/UILanguage.description: The language of the Windows Setup screens. The media must include it. Leave it unset and Setup asks or uses the media language.

SetupUILanguage/WillShowUI.description: When Setup shows its language page. OnError shows it only if the language is missing. Leave it unset for OnError.

valueHelp.Always: Setup always shows the language page.
valueHelp.onError: Setup shows the page only when the language is missing or wrong.

Interfaces/Interface/Identifier.description: Which network adapter these settings apply to: its connection name such as Ethernet, or its MAC address such as 00-15-5D-01-02-03. A MAC address is safer when there are several adapters. A wrong name means nothing is applied.

Interfaces/Interface/Ipv4Settings/DhcpEn.description: Whether the adapter gets its IPv4 address from DHCP. Turn it off when you set a static address below. Leave it unset to keep DHCP on.

valueHelp.true: The adapter gets its IPv4 address from DHCP.
valueHelp.false: DHCP is off; use the static addresses below.

Interfaces/Interface/Ipv6Settings/DhcpEn.description: Whether the adapter asks DHCPv6 for an IPv6 address. Most networks use router advertisements instead. Leave it unset for the Windows default.

valueHelp.true: The adapter asks DHCPv6 for an address.
valueHelp.false: DHCPv6 is off.

Interfaces/Interface/Ipv4Settings/Metric.description: The interface metric for IPv4; lower numbers are preferred when several adapters can reach a network. Typical values run from 5 for fast links to 50 for slow ones. Leave it unset so Windows picks it from the link speed.

Interfaces/Interface/Ipv6Settings/Metric.description: The interface metric for IPv6; lower numbers are preferred when several adapters can reach a network. Typical values run from 5 for fast links to 50 for slow ones. Leave it unset so Windows picks it from the link speed.

Interfaces/Interface/UnicastIpAddresses/.description: A static address with its prefix length, such as 192.168.10.20/24 or 2001:db8::20/64. Turn DHCP off for the adapter when you set one. Each address needs a unique key.
A unique number for this address entry, starting at 1. Windows only uses it to tell the entries apart. The studio fills it in for you.

Interfaces/Interface/Routes/Route/Prefix.description: The destination network of the route in CIDR form. Use 0.0.0.0/0 for the default gateway. Each route needs a unique identifier.

Interfaces/Interface/Routes/Route/NextHo.description: The gateway address that traffic for this route goes to. It must be on the same subnet as the adapter address. For the default route it is the router of the network.

Interfaces/Interface/Routes/Route/Identi.description: A unique number for this route entry, often starting at 0 or 1. Windows only uses it to tell routes apart. The studio fills it in for you.

Interfaces/Interface/Routes/Route/Metric.description: The route metric; lower numbers win when several routes match the same prefix. Leave it unset for the default. Only set it when you have more than one gateway.

DNSDomain.description: The primary DNS suffix of the computer, added to short names when resolving. Domain members get it from the domain automatically. Leave it empty unless the computer stays in a workgroup.

UseDomainNameDevolution.description: Whether Windows also tries parent domains of the suffix when resolving short names. For example a.b.example.com also tries b.example.com. Leave it unset to keep devolution on.

valueHelp.true: Parent domains of the suffix are tried too.
valueHelp.false: Only the exact suffixes are tried.

DNSSuffixSearchOrder/DomainName/Value.description: A DNS suffix added to short names, in the order of the keys. Use it when users type short names from several domains. Each suffix needs a unique key.

Interfaces/Interface/Identifier.description: Which network adapter these DNS settings apply to: its connection name or its MAC address. It must match the adapter name in the installed system. A wrong name means nothing is applied.

Interfaces/Interface/DNSServerSearchOrde.description: A DNS server address for this adapter, tried in key order. Domain members should point at a domain controller first. Each server needs a unique key starting at 1.

Interfaces/Interface/DNSDomain.description: A DNS suffix specific to this adapter. It is added to short names resolved through it. Leave it empty to use the primary suffix only.

Interfaces/Interface/EnableAdapterDomain.description: Whether Windows registers the adapter suffix name and address in DNS. Turn it on when other computers must find this one by the adapter suffix. Leave it unset for the default.

valueHelp.true: The adapter registers its suffix name in DNS.
valueHelp.false: The adapter does not register its suffix name.

Interfaces/Interface/DisableDynamicUpdat.description: Stops the adapter from registering its name and address in DNS. Note that true turns registration OFF. Leave it unset so the computer registers itself, which domain members need.

valueHelp.true: Dynamic DNS registration is OFF for this adapter.
valueHelp.false: The adapter registers its name and address in DNS.

Identification/JoinDomain.description: The DNS name of the domain to join during specialize. The computer must reach a domain controller through DNS at that time. Leave it empty to stay in a workgroup.

Identification/JoinWorkgroup.description: The workgroup to join instead of a domain. Use it only when you do not join a domain. Leave it empty for WORKGROUP.

Identification/MachineObjectOU.description: The organizational unit, as a distinguished name, where the computer account is created. The join account needs rights to create computers there. Leave it empty for the default Computers container.

Identification/UnsecureJoin.description: Joins with a computer account that was created in advance, using the machine password instead of user credentials. Leave Credentials empty when you turn it on. Leave it unset for a normal join.

valueHelp.true: Join with a pre-created computer account and the machine password; no user credentials.
valueHelp.false: Join with the user credentials below.

Identification/MachinePassword.description: The one-time password of a computer account created in advance, used with UnsecureJoin. It is written in plain text. Leave it empty for a normal join.

risk.reason: Stored in plain text in the answer file.

Identification/DebugJoin.description: Stops Setup when the domain join fails, so you can read the logs before the computer moves on. Use it while you test a deployment. Leave it unset so Setup continues in a workgroup.

valueHelp.true: Setup stops on a join failure for troubleshooting.
valueHelp.false: Setup continues if the join fails.

Identification/TimeoutPeriodInMinutes.description: How long Windows keeps trying to reach the domain before it gives up, from 5 to 60 minutes. Raise it for slow networks. Leave it unset for 15 minutes.

Identification/Credentials/Username.description: An account allowed to join computers to the domain. Use a delegated join account, not a domain administrator. It is written to the answer file.

Identification/Credentials/Domain.description: The domain of the join account, as a NetBIOS or DNS name. It is usually the domain you join. Leave it empty only with UnsecureJoin.

Identification/Credentials/Password.description: The password of the join account. It is written in plain text, so use a delegated account that can only join computers. Leave it empty only with UnsecureJoin.

Identification/Provisioning/AccountData.description: An offline domain join blob made with djoin /provision, pasted as one line. It lets the computer join without reaching a domain controller during Setup. Treat it like a password, because it holds the computer account secret.

risk.reason: The blob contains the computer account password.

OfflineIdentification/Provisioning/Accou.description: An offline domain join blob made with djoin /provision, applied in the offlineServicing pass. It lets the computer join without reaching a domain controller. Treat it like a password, because it holds the computer account secret.

risk.reason: The blob contains the computer account password.

EnableLUA.description: Turns User Account Control on or off. With UAC off every administrator runs everything with full rights and many apps stop working. Leave it unset to keep UAC on.

valueHelp.true: User Account Control is on: administrators confirm elevation.
valueHelp.false: User Account Control is off: every admin process runs elevated without asking.

risk.reason: Disabling UAC removes a key security boundary and breaks Store apps.

fDenyTSConnections.description: Allows or blocks Remote Desktop connections to this computer. The name is inverted: false allows connections and true denies them. Leave it unset to keep Remote Desktop blocked, which is the default.

valueHelp.false: Remote Desktop connections are allowed.
valueHelp.true: Remote Desktop connections are blocked.

risk.reason: Remote Desktop listens on TCP 3389; also open the firewall rule group and keep Network Level Authentication on.

UserAuthentication.description: Requires Network Level Authentication, so users sign in before a Remote Desktop session starts. Keep it on unless very old clients must connect. Leave it unset to use the Windows default.

valueHelp.0: Network Level Authentication is not required.

risk.reason: Without NLA the sign-in screen is exposed to anyone who can reach the port.

SecurityLayer.description: How the Remote Desktop server proves its identity before the session starts. TLS is the most secure; Negotiate picks TLS when the client supports it. Leave it unset for Negotiate.

valueHelp.0: RDP security only, without TLS server authentication.
valueHelp.1: Negotiate: use TLS when the client supports it.

risk.reason: Without TLS the server identity is not verified.

IEHardenAdmin.description: Keeps Internet Explorer Enhanced Security Configuration on for administrators. Turning it off lets admins browse freely from the server, which is a security cost. Leave it unset to keep it on.

valueHelp.true: Enhanced Security Configuration is on for administrators.
valueHelp.false: Enhanced Security Configuration is off for administrators.

risk.reason: Browsing from a server as an administrator is risky.

IEHardenUser.description: Keeps Internet Explorer Enhanced Security Configuration on for standard users. Turning it off lets users browse freely from the server. Leave it unset to keep it on.

valueHelp.true: Enhanced Security Configuration is on for users.
valueHelp.false: Enhanced Security Configuration is off for users.

risk.reason: Browsing from a server is risky.

DoNotOpenServerManagerAtLogon.description: Stops Server Manager from opening every time an administrator signs in. Common for servers managed remotely or with scripts. Leave it unset to open Server Manager.

valueHelp.true: Server Manager does not open at sign-in.
valueHelp.false: Server Manager opens at sign-in.

SkipAutoActivation.description: Stops Windows from activating automatically over the internet after Setup. Use it for labs, offline builds or when KMS activation happens later. Leave it unset to activate automatically.

valueHelp.true: Windows does not try to activate automatically.
valueHelp.false: Windows activates automatically when it can.

SkipRearm.description: Whether sysprep resets the activation grace period when it generalizes the image. Windows allows only a few resets, so set 1 while you build and capture an image repeatedly. Leave it unset to reset as normal.

valueHelp.0: The licensing state is reset to out of box when generalizing.
valueHelp.1: The licensing state is kept; the reset count is not used.

CEIPEnabled.description: Turns the Customer Experience Improvement Program on or off. It sends usage data to Microsoft on older releases. Leave it unset for the Windows default.

valueHelp.0: The program is off; no usage data is sent.
valueHelp.1: The program is on; usage data is sent.

DisableWER.description: Turns Windows Error Reporting off or on. With it off, crash reports are not collected or sent. Leave it unset to keep error reporting on.

valueHelp.0: Windows Error Reporting is on.

valueHelp.2: Ask before sending anything except basic app details such as name and version.
valueHelp.3: Send basic app details and data that is likely safe; ask for the rest.
valueHelp.4: Send all error reports without asking.

PreferredPlan.description: The GUID of the power plan to make active. Pick a built-in plan or the GUID of a custom plan you import. Leave it unset for Balanced.

risk.reason: Clearing the TPM destroys keys, including BitLocker recovery protection.

ClearTpm.description: Clears the TPM during Setup so it starts with no owner and no keys. Only use it on devices you are repurposing. Leave it unset to keep the TPM as it is (0).

AllowInsecureGuestAuth.description: Allows connecting to file shares that accept guest access without a password. Modern Windows blocks this because it exposes users to rogue servers. Leave it unset to keep it blocked.

valueHelp.0: Guest access to file shares is blocked.
valueHelp.1: Guest access to file shares is allowed.

risk.reason: Unauthenticated SMB guest access lets rogue servers pose as file shares.

valueHelp.true: The Windows Recovery Environment is removed after Setup.
valueHelp.false: The Windows Recovery Environment is kept on the disk.

risk.reason: Without Windows RE you cannot use startup repair or reset this PC.

valueHelp.0: System Restore is on and creates restore points.

risk.reason: No restore points can be used to undo bad changes.

DisableAntiSpyware.description: Turns Microsoft Defender Antivirus off. Only do this when another managed antivirus is installed, because Windows is otherwise unprotected. Leave it unset to keep Defender on.

valueHelp.true: Microsoft Defender Antivirus is turned off.
valueHelp.false: Microsoft Defender Antivirus stays on.

risk.reason: The computer has no antivirus unless another product is installed.

Scan/ScheduleTime.description: The local time of day when the scheduled full scan starts. It is stored as minutes past midnight. Leave it unset for 02:00.

Scan/ScanParameters.description: Which kind of scan the scheduled scan runs. A quick scan checks common places; a full scan checks every file. Leave it unset for quick.

Scan/ScheduleDay.description: Which day the scheduled scan runs. Pick a day when the device is on but not busy. Leave it unset for never (8).

valueHelp.0: Every day.

FirewallGroups/FirewallGroup/Group.description: The name of a built-in firewall rule group to turn on or off, such as Remote Desktop or File and Printer Sharing. Use the English group name or its resource id. A wrong name is ignored.

FirewallGroups/FirewallGroup/Active.description: Whether every rule in the group is turned on. Turn it on to open the ports the group covers, for example Remote Desktop. Leave it unset to keep the group as Windows ships it.

valueHelp.true: The rules in the group are turned on (the ports open).
valueHelp.false: The rules in the group are turned off.

FirewallGroups/FirewallGroup/Profile.description: Which network profiles the group change applies to. Use all for servers that may move between networks. Leave it unset for all profiles.

valueHelp.all: The change applies to every profile.

FirewallGroups/FirewallGroup/Key.description: A unique name for this entry, for example RemoteDesktop. Windows only uses it to tell the entries apart. Each entry in the list needs its own key.

Reseal/Mode.description: Where the computer goes after this pass: audit mode for more customization or the out-of-box experience for the end user. Use OOBE for the final image. Leave it unset for the Windows default.

valueHelp.Audit: The computer restarts into audit mode.
valueHelp.OOBE: The computer restarts into the out-of-box experience.

Reseal/ForceShutdownNow.description: Shuts the computer down right after reseal instead of restarting. Use it before you capture or ship the disk. Leave it unset to restart.

valueHelp.true: The computer shuts down after reseal.
valueHelp.false: The computer restarts after reseal.

valueHelp.true: The computer shuts down after the generalize pass.
valueHelp.false: The computer restarts after the generalize pass.

valueHelp.0: Unknown form factor.
valueHelp.5: Convertible notebook with a swivel or fold-back keyboard.
valueHelp.7: All-in-one desktop with an attached display.
valueHelp.8: Stick PC that plugs into a TV.

DeviceForm.description: Tells Windows what kind of device this is, such as a desktop, laptop or kiosk. Windows uses it to tune the interface and for telemetry. Leave it unset so the firmware reports it.

ExtendOSPartition/Size.description: How many megabytes to add to the Windows partition. Leave it unset with Extend on to use all free space. The partition must be NTFS.

AuditComputerName/MustReboot.description: Restarts the computer right after it takes the audit mode name, so the name is in effect. Use it when later audit commands depend on the name. Leave it unset to keep running without a restart.

valueHelp.true: The computer restarts right after the name changes.
valueHelp.false: The computer keeps running; the name applies at the next restart.

AuditComputerName/Name.description: A computer name to use while the image is in audit mode. It does not carry into the final installation. Leave it empty for a random name.

Generalize/Mode.description: Where the computer goes after the generalize pass: audit mode or the out-of-box experience. Use OOBE for an image you will ship. Leave it unset for OOBE.

valueHelp.Audit: The computer starts in audit mode.
valueHelp.OOBE: The computer starts the out-of-box experience.

ExtendOSPartition/Extend.description: Grows the Windows partition into free space at the end of the disk during specialize. Use it when the image was captured from a smaller disk. Leave it unset to keep the size.

valueHelp.true: The Windows partition grows into the free space.
valueHelp.false: The partition keeps its size.

SanPolicy.description: Which newly found disks Windows brings online automatically. Use 2 on servers with shared SAN disks so another server cannot corrupt them. Leave it unset to bring all disks online (1).

valueHelp.2: Disks on a shared bus (SCSI, iSCSI, Fibre Channel, SAS) stay offline.
valueHelp.3: No new disk is brought online automatically.

valueHelp.true: Installed drivers are kept through sysprep generalize.
valueHelp.false: Device drivers are removed by sysprep generalize.

valueHelp.true: Devices that are not detected stay installed after the next specialize pass.
valueHelp.false: Devices that are not detected are removed in the next specialize pass.
Start appears right away while app registration continues in the background.

valueHelp.Auto: The computer becomes a browser only when the subnet needs one.

valueHelp.0: No sound plays for photos and recordings.
valueHelp.1-100: A sound plays at this volume for photos and recordings.

valueHelp.false: Navigation hints appear when the mouse hovers near a menu edge.

valueHelp.true: An error appears when the remote cannot start Media Center.
valueHelp.false: No error appears when the remote cannot start Media Center.

BytesDecryptedInDiskRequestOverhead.description: How many bytes BitLocker may decrypt for one disk request, a performance tuning value. Tune it only when testing shows a BitLocker throughput problem on that hardware. Leave it unset for 524,288 bytes.

MaxCryptoRequestsPerIo.description: The most encryption requests BitLocker splits one disk operation into. Tune it only when testing shows a BitLocker throughput problem on that hardware. Leave it unset for 5.

MaxDecryptRequests.description: The most decrypt requests BitLocker runs at the same time; 0 means no limit. Tune it only when testing shows a BitLocker throughput problem on that hardware. Leave it unset for 0.

MaxEncryptRequests.description: The most encrypt requests BitLocker runs at the same time. Tune it only when testing shows a BitLocker throughput problem on that hardware. Leave it unset for 2.

SlicedEncryptionInPlace.description: Whether BitLocker encrypts large requests in place or copies them to a second buffer first. Tune it only when testing shows a BitLocker throughput problem on that hardware. Leave it unset for in place (1).

SlicedEncryptionMinSize.description: The smallest request, in bytes, that BitLocker splits into slices. Tune it only when testing shows a BitLocker throughput problem on that hardware. Leave it unset for 524,288 bytes.

SlicedEncryptionRequestsMax.description: The most slices BitLocker processes at the same time. Tune it only when testing shows a BitLocker throughput problem on that hardware. Leave it unset for 1.

WriteIoAggregateMaxSize.description: The largest combined write, in bytes, that BitLocker builds from small writes. Tune it only when testing shows a BitLocker throughput problem on that hardware. Leave it unset for the default, which depends on the disk type.

WriteIoAggregateMinSize.description: The smallest write, in bytes, that BitLocker combines with others. Tune it only when testing shows a BitLocker throughput problem on that hardware. Leave it unset for the default, which depends on the disk type.

WriteSubrequestLength.description: The size, in bytes, of each part when BitLocker splits a large write. Tune it only when testing shows a BitLocker throughput problem on that hardware. Leave it unset for 524,288 bytes.

InPlaceCrypto.description: Whether BitLocker may encrypt in place while double buffering is on. Tune it only when testing shows a BitLocker throughput problem on that hardware. Leave it unset to keep it off (0).

ModifiedWriteMaximum.description: The most modified pages BitLocker writes in one go. Tune it only when testing shows a BitLocker throughput problem on that hardware. Leave it unset for 4.

ReadDoubleBuffering.description: Whether BitLocker reads into a second buffer before decrypting. Tune it only when testing shows a BitLocker throughput problem on that hardware. Leave it unset to keep it off (0).

PreventDeviceEncryption.description: Stops Windows from turning on automatic device encryption (BitLocker) on supported hardware. Use it when you manage BitLocker yourself or must avoid encryption on test machines. Leave it unset so Windows can encrypt the device.

valueHelp.true: Automatic device encryption is not turned on.

Interfaces/Interface/NetbiosOptions.description: Turns NetBIOS over TCP/IP on or off for this adapter. Turning it off reduces old broadcast name traffic on modern networks. Leave it unset to follow DHCP.

valueHelp.0: Use the setting from DHCP.

Size.description: How much memory the file server uses for sharing. Choose 3 for file servers and 1 for computers that rarely share files. Leave it unset for 3.

valueHelp.3: Use more memory for file sharing throughput.

LmAnnounce.description: Makes the computer announce itself to old LAN Manager browse lists. Modern networks do not need it. Leave it unset to stay quiet.

valueHelp.true: The server sends LAN Manager announcements.
valueHelp.false: The server does not announce itself.

TCGSecurityActivationDisabled.description: Stops Windows from turning on hardware encryption for self-encrypting drives. Use it when another tool manages those drives. Leave it unset so Windows can manage them.
